verdict.causeFiltered: The target dropped the connection: the port is filtered, which means a firewall or a security group on the target — not a dead service.
verdict.causeRefused: The host answered and refused the connection, so nothing is listening on that port.
verdict.causeDns: The name did not resolve, so the problem is the name or its DNS records, not the service.
verdict.causeSshKey: The SSH server rejected the key it was offered, so this is the SSH key for that server, not the command.
verdict.causeApiKey: The provider rejected the API key (401), so the key stored in Settings is wrong or expired.
verdict.causePermission: The command was right but this identity may not run it: the system refused the operation (EACCES / root required).
verdict.causeForbidden: The server understood the request and refused it with 403: the token or the role lacks this permission.
verdict.causeDiskFull: The filesystem is full (ENOSPC), so the write did not happen.
verdict.causeMissingTool: A program this command needs is not installed on this machine.
verdict.causeMissingToolNamed: {{tool}} is not installed on this machine, so every command that calls it fails the same way.
verdict.causeTimeout: That step was too slow: it hit its time limit and the output names no other error.
verdict.causeStalled: Several steps made no progress and no error was recorded — this is the loop itself.
verdict.causeTurnBudget: The turn used its whole time window; no step failed.
verdict.causeUnknown: The run stopped and recorded no specific cause: the output matches no known failure pattern.
verdict.nextFiltered: Open the port on the target for this machine's address (ufw or the cloud security group), or run the same test from the other host to prove it is the network between them.
verdict.nextRefused: Start the service that should listen on that port, or check with `ss -ltnp` which port it really listens on, then send the same command again.
verdict.nextDns: Check the host name and its DNS record (or /etc/hosts), then run it once the name resolves.
verdict.nextSshKey: Fix the SSH key for that server: the key path and its permissions, and that the public key is in that account's authorized_keys.
verdict.nextApiKey: Replace the API key for that provider in Settings and run the step again; the old key will keep returning 401.
verdict.nextPermission: Run the same command with the privilege it needs (sudo, or a user that owns the path); a different command fails in exactly the same place.
verdict.nextForbidden: Use a token or a role that holds this permission and send the same request again; the command itself is fine.
verdict.nextDiskFull: Free space first (df -h, then delete or rotate what filled the disk) and only then repeat the write; repeating it now fails in exactly the same way.
verdict.nextMissingTool: Install the missing program on that host and run the same command again.
verdict.nextMissingToolNamed: Install {{tool}} on that host (your package manager, or the vendor's own installer) and run the same command again.
verdict.nextTimeout: Run a narrower version of that step (one file, one host, a smaller range) or give it a longer budget; the same command with the same limit hits the same wall.
verdict.nextStalled: Change the instruction, not the wording: name the exact file or command, or say which alternative to try next.
verdict.nextTurnBudget: Continue from where it stopped; nothing failed, the clock simply ran out.
verdict.nextUnknown: Read the trace above and give a narrower instruction than the one that stalled; the run has no evidence that could name a cause.
verdict.causeUpstreamBlocked: The host is up and that port is still dropped from another machine: nothing on the host itself can be the cause, because the block is above it — a security group or an upstream ACL at the hosting provider.
verdict.nextUpstreamBlocked: Open inbound TCP 22 for the source address in the hosting provider's firewall panel (the provider the server's PTR names; the host's own ufw and iptables were clean, so the rule has to go there). Or transfer the project through this computer instead — pull it from the source and push it on to the target — because the route from here may not be blocked even when the other one is.
verdict.causeBlockedLocally: The TCP connect to that port was dropped, and nothing in the evidence proves the host itself is up: reachability is unknown, so this is not yet evidence about anyone above it.
verdict.nextBlockedLocally: Prove the host is up first — open a console session on it, or ping it from this machine — and only then retest that port from the same machine. A filtered result against a host nobody checked the state of says nothing about who blocks it.
verdict.causeRepeatedEvidence: The last two steps re-ran probes whose answers were already known: the output did not change, so nothing new was learned and the run was circling the same question instead of the problem.
verdict.nextRepeatedEvidence: Say in one sentence what is already established and what it rules out, then change the question — a different target, a different measurement, or the route through this computer — rather than re-running the same probe.
verdict.causeSessionDropped: The SSH session to that server is gone, so the command never ran.
verdict.nextSessionDropped: Reconnect that server and retry the step; or switch this project to another server.

target.incomplete: Only the verifications that ran are covered here. A migration is confirmed when both the files and the database have been compared.
target.sourceServer: Source (where the files are read from)

target.steps: Steps, in order, with what each must produce
target.dbBody: The dump is taken inside the container on the source, moved as one file, and restored on the target. The table count and the row counts of a bounded sample decide whether the restore is complete â€” a partial restore fails loudly.
target.needDryRun: A dry run must pass (PASS) before the restore can run.
target.dryBanner: Dry run: these are the exact commands. Nothing has been written â€” no directory, no dump, no restore.
target.dbCancelled: Cancelled. The dump on both ends is kept, so running it again resumes â€” nothing was restored.
target.dbVerification: After: {{tables}} tables, {{sampled}} sampled row counts compared, dump sha256 {{digest}}.
target.bringUpBody: A checklist, not a conversation: .env, dependencies, build, two PM2 apps, the nginx sites, the certificates and a health check on each port. Every step shows its command, what success looks like, and a verdict â€” and it can be cancelled and resumed.
target.domains: Domains that need a certificate â€” their DNS must already point at the target
target.resume: Continue from the steps that passed
target.stopping: Stopping at the next step boundary — the steps that already passed are kept.
target.runCancelled: Cancelled. The steps that passed are kept â€” Continue resumes from there instead of starting over.
target.envReport: .env keys (presence only â€” a value is never read)
